title: Behavioral-Delta Gate for Batch/Cache Config Recommendations
creator: Sofia Li
description: Implement a probabilistic, behavioral-delta acceptance gate that evaluates batch/caching configuration recommendations produced by the cost-optimizer. The gate must detect semantic and functional regressions introduced by config changes (e.g., higher batching or more aggressive prefix reuse) before automated apply. It should operate as a staged acceptability check: smokebench -> stratified micro-evals -> human review for marginal cases, and provide deterministic rollback triggers.
background: Our cost-autotuner generates recommended batch sizes and caching heuristics that reduce per-token cost but can subtly alter model output behavior (repetition, truncated completions, degraded instruction-following). Previous incidents show subtle regressions evaded single-metric checks. This task builds an ensemble acceptance harness that correlates embedding-level drift, functional test pass-rate, and user-facing signal regressions to decide safe apply or rollback.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible smokebench that runs a recommended config in a shadow environment and computes: median token cost delta, 95th-quantile latency, and embedding cosine drift vs baseline (per-route)
Stratified micro-eval suite covering: instruction-following (instruction prompts set), slot-filling accuracy, safe completion checks, and conversational coherence with automated scoring
A probabilistic decision function that outputs one of {ACCEPT, REVIEW, REJECT} with explainability: top contributing metrics and cohort-level deltas
Rollback triggers: automatic rollback if post-apply live telemetry shows >5% drop in route-level functional pass-rate or average embedding similarity below threshold within 2 hours
Human review workflow integration: flagged REVIEW cases create a ticket with diffs, representative golden prompts, and quick links to side-by-side output diffs
End-to-end test verifying canary apply to 1% traffic, metric collection, decision result, and automated rollback on simulated regression
Documentation page with runbook, thresholds, and instructions for manual override
design_decisions: Use embedding-cosine (OpenAI-style high-dim embed) + token-level log-probability delta as primary detectors rather than solely lexical metrics (BLEU/ROUGE)
Stratify evaluation by traffic cohorts: low-context (<256 tokens), medium (256-1024), long (>1024) to capture sequence-length-dependent regressions
Ensemble scoring: weighted combination of semantic drift (cosine), functional pass-rate (binary tests), and regression risk score from historical rollout models
Adopt probabilistic thresholds (p-values via bootstrap on paired differences) to avoid brittle static cutoffs
Shadow-run stage will use identical seeds and deterministic runtime kernel selection where possible to isolate config effects from nondeterminism
Human-in-the-loop for REVIEW outcomes; reviewers see canonical golden prompts, representative failures, aggregate metrics, and ability to mark accept/reject
implementation_notes: Extend existing cost-advisor service to emit a candidate-config artifact (JSON) with meta: route, model, expected p50/p95 improvements
Create a smokebench runner that can spin a dedicated smoke pod with candidate config and run paired request sets against baseline (reuse runtime dev infra)
Instrument new per-request tags for canary id and keep an operation id so post-apply telemetry correlates to the candidate run
Build micro-eval harness that pulls golden prompt corpus (stable S3 path) and runs head-to-head comparisons using current baseline model variant
Implement statistical evaluator: paired bootstrap to estimate confidence interval for mean semantic shift and a binomial test for pass-rate changes
Expose decision API that returns explainable fields: metric_deltas, cohort_breakdown, p_values, and suggested_action
Add a compact UI summary in Console Rollouts with quick links to full diffs and human review button
Plan for a feature flag to gate auto-apply behavior while we iterate on thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for decision logic covering edge cases: small sample sizes, missing metrics, and tie-breaking rules
Integration test: shadow-run vs baseline with synthetic prompts containing controlled perturbations to validate detector sensitivity
Canary simulation: simulate a 1% traffic apply in staging and inject a 7% functional-regression signal to verify automatic rollback
Performance test: ensure smokebench runs within acceptable time (target < 30m per config) with parallelization
Fuzz tests: randomized golden prompt mutations to ensure ensemble scoring is robust to noisy inputs
Human review dry-run: internal reviewers to approve/reject a set of historical candidate configs to validate workflow ergonomics
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement smokebench + decision API, run 50 retrospective candidate-configs and confirm decisions align with historical outcomes
Phase 2 (canary): enable auto-apply for low-risk routes with 0.5-1% traffic and monitor for 48h before scaling up
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): expand to P0/P1 routes with additional logging and extended observability
Emergency rollback policy: immediate global rollback command with a 15-minute SLA for operator to intervene
Human override: allow product lead to override and pin configs with justification recorded
monitoring: Dashboards: per-candidate summary (cost delta, semantic drift, pass-rate change, decision), cohort-level breakdown
Alerts: above-threshold regression detected post-apply (e.g., >5% functional drop on 1-hour rolling window) triggers P0 alert
Audit logs: store candidate-config artifacts, decision payloads, human reviewer votes, and final applied config
Retention: keep full eval traces for 90 days for audit and debugging
Drift watchlist: continuous background job that re-evaluates last N applied configs against fresh golden prompt samples weekly
dependencies: Console team API for rollouts (depend on console-2026.04 release schedule)
Storage: stable S3 path for golden prompt corpus and representative traffic samples
Auth: reviewer SSO/SAML permission to mark decisions
